metadata.title: Beyond Locality-Sensitive Hashing
metadata.authors: Alexandr Andoni, Piotr Indyk, Huy L. Nguyen, Ilya Razenshteyn

nodes.name: $(c,r)$-approximate near neighbor problem (ANN)
nodes.statement: Given a set $P$ of points in metric space $(X,D)$ and failure probability $f$, build a data structure that, on query $q$, if some $p \in P$ has $D(p,q) \le r$, returns $p' \in P$ with $D(p',q) \le cr$ with probability $\ge 1-f$.

nodes.name: $(r_1,r_2,p_1,p_2)$-sensitive hash family
nodes.statement: A family $\mathcal{H}$ on $(X,D)$ is $(r_1,r_2,p_1,p_2)$-sensitive if for all $x,y \in X$: $D(x,y) \le r_1 \Rightarrow \Pr_{h\sim\mathcal{H}}[h(x)=h(y)] \ge p_1$ and $D(x,y) \ge r_2 \Rightarrow \Pr[h(x)=h(y)] \le p_2$.

nodes.name: Tensor power $\mathcal{H}^{\otimes k}$
nodes.statement: For a hash family $\mathcal{H}$ and $k \in \mathbb{N}$, sample $\mathcal{H}^{\otimes k}$ by drawing $h_1,\dots,h_k \sim \mathcal{H}$ independently and mapping $x \mapsto (h_1(x),\dots,h_k(x))$.

nodes.name: Sensitivity of tensor power
nodes.statement: If $\mathcal{H}$ is $(r_1,r_2,p_1,p_2)$-sensitive, then $\mathcal{H}^{\otimes k}$ is $(r_1,r_2,p_1^k,p_2^k)$-sensitive.

nodes.name: LSH-to-ANN reduction
nodes.statement: If a $(r,cr,p_1,p_2)$-sensitive family exists with $\rho = \ln(1/p_1)/\ln(1/p_2)$, there is a $(c,r)$-ANN data structure using $O(n^\rho/p_1)$ distance computations per query, $O(n^\rho/p_1 \cdot \lceil \log_{1/p_2} n \rceil)$ hash evaluations, and $O(n^{1+\rho}/p_1)$ words of space.

nodes.name: Ball-carving LSH (Andoni-Indyk)
nodes.statement: For sufficiently large $d,n$ there is a hash family $\mathcal{H}$ on $\ell_2^d$ whose collision probability depends only on $\|u-v\|$, with $p(1) \ge L = \frac{A}{2\sqrt{t}}(1+\eps+8\eps^2)^{-t/2}$ and $p(c) \le U(c) = 2(1+c^2\eps)^{-t/2}$, where $t=\log^{2/3} n$ and $\eps = \Theta(t^{-1/2})$.

nodes.name: Baseline $\ell_2$ ANN with $\rho = 1/c^2$
nodes.statement: There is a data structure for $(c,r)$-ANN in $\ell_2^d$ with preprocessing time/space $O_c(n^{1+1/c^2 + o_c(1)} + nd)$ and query time $O_c(d\, n^{1/c^2 + o_c(1)})$.

nodes.name: Proof of CP11.1
nodes.statement: By rescaling assume $r=1$; combine Theorem~\ref{lsh_to_nn} with Theorem~\ref{ball_carving} and check $L = n^{-o_c(1)}$ and $\ln(1/L)/\ln(1/U(c)) \le 1/c^2 + o_c(1)$.

nodes.name: Gaussian tail bound
nodes.statement: For every $t > 0$: $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}(\frac{1}{t}-\frac{1}{t^3})e^{-t^2/2} \le \Pr_{X\sim N(0,1)}[X \ge t] \le \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \cdot \frac{1}{t} e^{-t^2/2}$.

nodes.name: Johnson-Lindenstrauss dimension reduction
nodes.statement: For every $d \in \mathbb{N}$ and $\eps,\delta > 0$ there is a distribution over linear maps $A:\mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}^{O(\log(1/\delta)/\eps^2)}$ with $\Pr_A[\|Ax\| \in (1\pm\eps)\|x\|] \ge 1-\delta$ for every $x$, samplable in $O(d\log(1/\delta)/\eps^2)$ time.

nodes.name: Jung's theorem
nodes.statement: Every subset of $\mathbb{R}^d$ with diameter $\Delta$ can be enclosed in a ball of radius $\Delta/\sqrt{2}$.
conclusions: $S$ is enclosed in a ball of radius $\Delta/\sqrt{2}$
nodes.origin_citation: Matousek, Lectures on Discrete Geometry, Exercise 1.3.5

nodes.name: Idealized Gaussian LSH on a sphere
nodes.statement:
For sufficiently large $c$, every $
u \ge 1/2$ and $1/2 \le \eta \le 
u$, there is a $(1,c,p_1,p_2)$-sensitive LSH family for $\eta c \cdot S^{d-1}$ with $p_1 = \exp(-o_{c,
u}(d))$ and $ho = (1- rac{1}{4\eta^2})\cdot rac{1}{c^2} + O_
u(1/c^3) + o_{c,
u}(1)$.
assumptions: Points lie on sphere $\eta c \cdot S^{d-1}$
conclusions: LSH family on $\eta c \cdot S^{d-1}$ is $(1,c,p_1,p_2)$-sensitive

nodes.name: Gaussian partitioning
nodes.statement: Random Gaussian partition of $\eta c \cdot S^{d-1}$ into halfspace caps $\{u : \langle u,w\rangle \ge \eta c \eps \sqrt{d}\}$ with i.i.d. Gaussian $w$, used to define the idealized LSH family $\mathcal{H}$.
output: Hash function $h:\eta c \cdot S^{d-1} \to \mathcal{P}$ mapping each point to its containing part

nodes.name: Initialize empty partition
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{P} \gets \emptyset$.

nodes.name: Cap-sampling loop
nodes.statement: While $\bigcup\mathcal{P} \ne \eta c \cdot S^{d-1}$, sample $w \sim N(0,1)^d$ and form the unclaimed cap $S \gets \{u \in \eta c \cdot S^{d-1} : \langle u,w\rangle \ge \eta c \eps \sqrt{d}\}\setminus\bigcup\mathcal{P}$.

nodes.name: Add nonempty cap to partition
nodes.statement: If $S \ne \emptyset$, add $S$ to $\mathcal{P}$.

nodes.name: Define hash function $h$
nodes.statement: Define $h$ to map a point $u \in \eta c \cdot S^{d-1}$ to the part of $\mathcal{P}$ containing it.

nodes.name: Proof of TP11.5 (idealized Gaussian LSH)
nodes.statement: Compute the collision probability via Gaussian-tail estimates (Lemmas \ref{numerator_up}, \ref{numerator_lo}); set $\eps = d^{-1/4}$; bound $\ln(1/p_1)$ and $\ln(1/p_2)$ in terms of $\tan^2(\alpha/2)$ for the angles corresponding to distances $1$ and $c$; obtain the stated $\rho$.

nodes.name: Express collision probability via Gaussian inner products
nodes.statement: For $u,v \in \eta c \cdot S^{d-1}$ at angle $\alpha$, write $\Pr[h(u)=h(v)]$ as a ratio of Gaussian-cap probabilities and reduce to two-dimensional Gaussian probabilities $\Pr[X \ge \eps\sqrt{d} \wedge \cos\alpha \cdot X - \sin\alpha \cdot Y \ge \eps\sqrt{d}]$ via Equation~(\ref{coll}).

nodes.name: Apply numerator bounds (Lemmas \ref{numerator_up}, \ref{numerator_lo})
nodes.statement: Combine the upper and lower bounds on $\Pr[X \ge \eps\sqrt{d} \wedge \cos\alpha\cdot X - \sin\alpha\cdot Y \ge \eps\sqrt{d}]$ to obtain $\ln(1/\Pr[h(u)=h(v)]) \approx \frac{\eps^2 d}{2}\tan^2(\alpha/2)$ (Lemma~\ref{closed_coll}).

nodes.name: Translate angle to Euclidean distance
nodes.statement: Use $\tan^2(\alpha/2) = \frac{\|u-v\|^2/(\eta c)^2}{4 - \|u-v\|^2/(\eta c)^2}$ to convert the closed-form collision-probability bound from angles to distances.

nodes.name: Set $\eps = d^{-1/4}$ and conclude
nodes.statement:
Plug $\eps = d^{-1/4}$ into the bounds for distances $1$ and $c$, obtaining $\ln(1/p_1) \le  rac{\sqrt{d}}{2}\cdot rac{1/(\eta c)^2}{4-1/(\eta c)^2}+O_{c,
u}(\ln d)$ and a matching lower bound for $\ln(1/p_2)$, hence $ho =  rac{4-1/\eta^2}{4-1/(\eta c)^2}\cdot rac{1}{c^2}+o_{c,
u}(1) = (1- rac{1}{4\eta^2}) rac{1}{c^2}+O_
u(1/c^3)+o_{c,
u}(1)$.

nodes.name: Numerator upper bound
nodes.statement: $\Pr_{X,Y \sim N(0,1)}[X \ge \eps\sqrt{d} \wedge \cos\alpha\cdot X - \sin\alpha\cdot Y \ge \eps\sqrt{d}] = O\left(\frac{e^{-\eps^2 d (1+\tan^2(\alpha/2))/2}}{\eps\sqrt{d}}\right)$.

nodes.name: Proof of LP11.3
nodes.statement: Bound the joint event by $(1+\cos\alpha)X - \sin\alpha\cdot Y \ge 2\eps\sqrt{d}$, recognize the linear combination as $\sqrt{2(1+\cos\alpha)}\cdot Z$ for $Z \sim N(0,1)$, then apply Lemma~\ref{gaussians} together with the identity $\frac{2}{1+\cos\alpha}=1+\tan^2(\alpha/2)$.

nodes.name: Numerator lower bound
nodes.statement: If $0 \le \alpha < \alpha_0 < \pi/2$ for a constant $\alpha_0$, then $\Pr_{X,Y\sim N(0,1)}[X \ge \eps\sqrt{d} \wedge \cos\alpha\cdot X - \sin\alpha\cdot Y \ge \eps\sqrt{d}] = \Omega\left(\frac{e^{-\eps^2 d(1+\tan^2(\alpha_0/2))/2}}{\eps^2 d \tan(\alpha_0/2)}\right)$.

nodes.name: Proof of LP11.4
nodes.statement: Lower-bound the joint event by the independent event $\{X \ge \eps\sqrt{d}\}\wedge\{Y \le -\tan(\alpha/2)\eps\sqrt{d}\}$ (which implies the original since $\cos\alpha,\sin\alpha > 0$ and $\alpha < \alpha_0 < \pi/2$); replace $\alpha$ by the constant $\alpha_0$; and apply Lemma~\ref{gaussians}.

nodes.name: Closed-form collision-probability bound
nodes.statement: For $u,v$ at angle $\alpha$ on $\eta c\cdot S^{d-1}$: $\ln(1/\Pr[h(u)=h(v)]) \ge \frac{\eps^2 d}{2}\tan^2(\alpha/2) - O(1)$, and if $\alpha < \alpha_0 < \pi/2$ constant, then $\ln(1/\Pr[h(u)=h(v)]) \le \frac{\eps^2 d}{2}\tan^2(\alpha_0/2) + \ln(\eps\sqrt{d}\tan(\alpha_0/2)) + O(1)$.

nodes.name: Non-idealized Gaussian LSH (spherical shell)
nodes.statement: For sufficiently large $c$, every $\nu \ge 1/2$ and $1/2 \le \eta \le \nu$ there is an LSH family $\mathcal{H}$ for the shell $\{x \in \mathbb{R}^d : \|x\| \in [\eta c-1, \eta c+1]\}$ with the conclusion of Theorem~\ref{gaussian_lsh} and with sample/store/query time $\exp(o(d))$ for every $k \in \mathbb{N}$.
assumptions: Points lie in the shell $\|x\| \in [\eta c-1, \eta c+1]$
conclusions: Family $\mathcal{H}$ satisfies the conclusion of Theorem~\ref{gaussian_lsh}
Sample, store and query in time $\exp(o(d))$ for every $k \in \mathbb{N}$

nodes.name: Proof of LP11.6
nodes.statement: Expand $\|u/\|u\| - v/\|v\|\|^2 = 2 - 2\langle u,v\rangle/(\|u\|\|v\|)$ and rewrite using $2\langle u,v\rangle = \|u\|^2+\|v\|^2-\|u-v\|^2$.

nodes.name: Proof of TP11.6
nodes.statement: Modify Algorithm~\ref{gaussian_partitioning} by (i) running the partitioning for $\exp(o(d))$ steps until the uncovered measure is $\le e^{-d}$ and (ii) normalizing $x$ to length $\eta c$ before evaluating $h$; bound the distance perturbation via Lemma~\ref{LP11.6} to recover the conclusion of Theorem~\ref{gaussian_lsh}.

nodes.name: Truncate the partitioning loop
nodes.statement: Replace the unbounded \textbf{while} loop with a fixed $\exp(o(d))$-step run, which by an $\eps$-net argument covers $\eta c \cdot S^{d-1}$ with probability $\ge 1-\exp(-d)$, giving the $\exp(o(d))$ sample/store/query bounds.

nodes.name: Normalize input to $\eta c$ before hashing
nodes.statement: Define $h$ on the shell by first normalizing $x$ to $\eta c \cdot x/\|x\|$, then applying the spherical hash from Theorem~\ref{gaussian_lsh}.

nodes.name: Bound distance distortion via LP11.6
nodes.statement: Using Lemma~\ref{LP11.6}, show that for $u,v$ in the shell with $\|u-v\|\le 1$: $(\eta c\cdot \|u/\|u\|-v/\|v\|\|)^2 \le 1+O_\nu(1/c)$, and with $\|u-v\|\ge c$: $(\eta c\cdot \|\cdot\|)^2 \ge c^2(1-O_\nu(1/c))$.

nodes.name: Conclude conclusion of TP11.5 transfers
nodes.statement: These distortion bounds preserve the parameters $p_1,\rho$ from Theorem~\ref{gaussian_lsh} up to $o_c(1)$, completing the proof.

nodes.name: Two-level hashing
nodes.statement: Two-level data structure for $(c,1)$-ANN in $\ell_2^d$: an outer ball-carving LSH partitions points into bounded-diameter buckets, and within each bucket a Gaussian LSH centered at the smallest enclosing ball is applied to spherical-shell layers indexed by $l$.
input: Parameters $\tau$ (diameter scale), $T$ (number of shells), $k$ (outer hash length), $\widetilde{k}_l$ (inner hash lengths)
output: Build: outer hash $h$, buckets $B_i$ with center $u_i$ and nearest neighbor $s_i$, shell datasets $\widetilde{P}_{il}$, inner hashes $\widetilde{h}_{il}$, inner buckets $\widetilde{B}_{ilj}$
Query: an approximate near neighbor $p \in P$ with $\|q-p\| \le c$, or $\perp$

nodes.name: Outer hashing into buckets
nodes.statement: Sample $h \sim \mathcal{H}_1^{\otimes k}$ from the ball-carving family (Theorem~\ref{ball_carving}); set $B_i \gets \{p \in P : h(p)=i\}$ for each bucket $i$.

nodes.name: Diameter-pruning inside each bucket
nodes.statement: For each bucket $B_i$, while there exist $p_1,p_2 \in B_i$ with $\|p_1-p_2\| > \tau c$, remove both. After pruning, $\mathrm{diam}(B_i) \le \tau c$.

nodes.name: Compute bucket center and nearest representative
nodes.statement: If $B_i \ne \emptyset$, let $u_i$ be the center of the smallest enclosing ball of $B_i$ and let $s_i \in B_i$ be the nearest neighbor of $u_i$.

nodes.name: Inner Gaussian hashing per shell
nodes.statement: For $l = 0,\ldots,T$: form the shell $\widetilde{P}_{il} \gets \{p-u_i : p \in B_i,\, c/2+l-1 \le \|p-u_i\| \le c/2+l+1\}$; sample $\widetilde{h}_{il} \sim \mathcal{H}_2^{\otimes \widetilde{k}_l}$ for $\eta = 1/2 + l/c$; set $\widetilde{B}_{ilj} \gets \{p \in \widetilde{P}_{il} : \widetilde{h}_{il}(p) = j\}$.

nodes.name: Query: locate outer bucket
nodes.statement: On query $q$, set $i \gets h(q)$; if $B_i = \emptyset$ return $\perp$.

nodes.name: Quick check via $s_i$
nodes.statement: If $\|q - s_i\| \le c$, return $s_i$.

nodes.name: Inner-shell scan
nodes.statement: For $l = 0,\ldots,T$ with $c/2+l-1 \le \|q-u_i\| \le c/2+l+1$: compute $j \gets \widetilde{h}_{il}(q-u_i)$ and check each $p \in \widetilde{B}_{ilj}$; if $\|q-(p+u_i)\| \le c$, return $p+u_i$.

nodes.name: Failure return
nodes.statement: If no candidate satisfies $\|q-\cdot\| \le c$, return $\perp$.

nodes.name: Choice of $T$
nodes.statement: $T = \left\lceil \frac{\tau c}{\sqrt{2}} - \frac{c}{2} \right\rceil + 1$.

nodes.name: Choice of outer hash length $k$
nodes.statement: Smallest positive integer $k$ with $(U(\tau c-1)/L)^k \le 1/(2n)$.

nodes.name: Choice of inner hash length $\widetilde{k}_l$
nodes.statement: $\widetilde{k}_l$ is the smallest positive integer with $U(c)^k \cdot \Pr_{\widetilde{h}\sim\mathcal{H}_2^{\otimes \widetilde{k}_l}}[\widetilde{h}(u)=\widetilde{h}(v)] \le 1/(3n)$ for all $u,v$ in the shell with $\|u-v\| \ge c$.

nodes.name: Bucket decomposes into shells
nodes.statement: After preprocessing, $B_i = \bigcup_{0 \le l \le T} \widetilde{P}_{il}$ for every $1 \le i \le m$.

nodes.name: Proof of LP11.7
nodes.statement: After lines 5--7 the diameter of $B_i$ is $\le \tau c$. By Jung's theorem (Theorem~\ref{jung}) the smallest enclosing ball has radius $\le \tau c/\sqrt{2}$, so for every $l > T$ the shell $\widetilde{P}_{il}$ is empty.

nodes.name: Disjunction probability bound
nodes.statement: If $\mathcal{U}$ and $\mathcal{V}$ are events with $\Pr[\mathcal{V}] < 1$, then $\Pr[\mathcal{U} \vee \mathcal{V}] \ge \Pr[\mathcal{U} \mid \neg\mathcal{V}]$.

nodes.name: Proof of LP11.8
nodes.statement:
Decompose $\Pr[\mathcal{U}\vee\mathcal{V}] = \Pr[\mathcal{V}] + \Pr[\mathcal{U}\mid
eg\mathcal{V}]\Pr[
eg\mathcal{V}]$ and bound $\Pr[\mathcal{V}] \ge \Pr[\mathcal{U}\mid
eg\mathcal{V}]\Pr[\mathcal{V}]$.

nodes.name: Upper bound on collision (far point)
nodes.statement: If $\|p-q\| \ge c$, then $\Pr[\mathcal{C}] \le 1/n$, where $\mathcal{C}$ is the event ``$p$ is iterated through in line 30 of Algorithm~\ref{two_level_hashing_alg}''.

nodes.name: Proof of LP11.9
nodes.statement: Since $\mathcal{C}$ implies $\mathcal{A}$, $\Pr[\mathcal{C}] = \Pr[\mathcal{A}]\Pr[\mathcal{C}\mid\mathcal{A}]$. Bound $\Pr[\mathcal{A}] \le U(c)^k$ via Theorem~\ref{ball_carving}; expand $\Pr[\mathcal{C}\mid\mathcal{A}]$ as a sum over at most $|W_q| \le 3$ shell indices; apply (\ref{choice_kl}) to conclude $\Pr[\mathcal{C}] \le 1/n$.

nodes.name: Lower bound on collision (near point)
nodes.statement: If $\|p-q\| \le 1$, then $\Pr[\mathcal{C}\vee\mathcal{D}] \ge n^{-(1-\frac{1}{2\tau^2}+\frac{1}{2\tau^4})\frac{1}{c^2} + O_\tau(1/c^3) + o_{c,\tau}(1)}$.

nodes.name: Proof of LP11.10
nodes.statement: Use Lemma~\ref{prob_ineq} to write $\Pr[\mathcal{C}\vee\mathcal{D}] \ge \Pr[\mathcal{A}]\Pr[\mathcal{B}\mid\mathcal{A}]\Pr[\mathcal{C}\mid\mathcal{A}\wedge\mathcal{B}\wedge\neg\mathcal{D}]$, then combine sub-lemmas (Lemmas~\ref{prob_a},~\ref{prob_b},~\ref{prob_c}) and the relations $L^k = n^{-1/(\tau^2 c^2)+\ldots}$ and $U(c)^k = n^{-1/\tau^2+\ldots}$ from~\cite{ai-nohaa-06}.

nodes.name: Chain inequality via Lemma~\ref{prob_ineq}
nodes.statement: Apply $\Pr[\mathcal{C}\vee\mathcal{D}] \ge \Pr[\mathcal{A}\wedge\mathcal{B}\wedge(\mathcal{C}\vee\mathcal{D})] = \Pr[\mathcal{A}]\Pr[\mathcal{B}\mid\mathcal{A}]\Pr[\mathcal{C}\vee\mathcal{D}\mid\mathcal{A}\wedge\mathcal{B}] \ge \Pr[\mathcal{A}]\Pr[\mathcal{B}\mid\mathcal{A}]\Pr[\mathcal{C}\mid\mathcal{A}\wedge\mathcal{B}\wedge\neg\mathcal{D}]$.

nodes.name: Lower bound $\Pr[\mathcal{A}]$ (Lemma~\ref{prob_a})
nodes.statement: By Theorem~\ref{ball_carving}, $\Pr[\mathcal{A}] = \Pr[h(p)=h(q)] \ge L^k$.

nodes.name: Lower bound $\Pr[\mathcal{B}\mid\mathcal{A}]$ (Lemma~\ref{prob_b})
nodes.statement: Using a union bound, Lemma~\ref{prob_a}, and choice~(\ref{choice_k}): $\Pr[\neg\mathcal{B}\mid\mathcal{A}] \le n(U(\tau c-1)/L)^k \le 1/2$.

nodes.name: Lower bound $\Pr[\mathcal{C}\mid\mathcal{A}\wedge\mathcal{B}\wedge\neg\mathcal{D}]$ (Lemma~\ref{prob_c})
nodes.statement: Show $p$ stays in $B_{h(q)}$ post-pruning, derive $\|p-u_{h(q)}\|, \|q-u_{h(q)}\| \ge c/2-1$, conclude that $p \in \widetilde{P}_{h(q)l}$ for some $l$ with $\eta = 1/2+l/c \le \tau/\sqrt{2}+O_\tau(1/c)$, then apply Theorem~\ref{non_ideal_gaussian_lsh} to bound $\Pr[\mathcal{C}\mid\mathcal{A}\wedge\mathcal{B}\wedge\neg\mathcal{D}] \ge (1/(3n U(c)^k))^{(1-1/(2\tau^2))/c^2 + O_\tau(1/c^3)+o_{c,\tau}(1)}$.

nodes.name: Plug in $L^k$ and $U(c)^k$ asymptotics
nodes.statement: From $U(x) = L^{x^2+o_x(1)}$ and the minimality of $k$ in (\ref{choice_k}): $L^k = n^{-1/(\tau^2 c^2)+O_\tau(1/c^3)+o_{c,\tau}(1)}$ and $U(c)^k = n^{-1/\tau^2+O_\tau(1/c)+o_{c,\tau}(1)}$.

nodes.name: Combine to bound $\Pr[\mathcal{C}\vee\mathcal{D}]$
nodes.statement: Substituting into the chain yields $\Pr[\mathcal{C}\vee\mathcal{D}] \ge n^{-(1-\frac{1}{2\tau^2}+\frac{1}{2\tau^4})\frac{1}{c^2}+O_\tau(1/c^3)+o_{c,\tau}(1)}$.

nodes.name: $\Pr[\mathcal{A}] \ge L^k$
nodes.statement: $\Pr[\mathcal{A}] = \Pr[h(p)=h(q)] \ge L^k$.

nodes.name: $\Pr[\mathcal{B}\mid\mathcal{A}] \ge 1/2$
nodes.statement: $\Pr[\mathcal{B}\mid\mathcal{A}] \ge 1/2$, where $\mathcal{B}$ is ``every $p' \in P$ with $\|p'-q\| > \tau c-1$ has $h(p') \ne h(q)$''.

nodes.name: $\Pr[\mathcal{C}\mid\mathcal{A}\wedge\mathcal{B}\wedge\neg\mathcal{D}]$ lower bound
nodes.statement: $\Pr[\mathcal{C}\mid\mathcal{A}\wedge\mathcal{B}\wedge\neg\mathcal{D}] \ge (1/(3n U(c)^k))^{(1-\frac{1}{2\tau^2})\frac{1}{c^2}+O_\tau(1/c^3)+o_{c,\tau}(1)}$.

nodes.name: Main theorem: improved $\rho$ for $\ell_2$ ANN
nodes.statement: There is a data structure for $(c,1)$-ANN in $\ell_2^d$ with preprocessing time $O_c(n^{2+\rho}+nd\log n)$, space $O_c(n^{1+\rho}+d\log n)$, query time $O_c(n^\rho+d\log n)$, and $\rho \le \frac{7/8}{c^2}+O(1/c^3)+o_c(1)$.

nodes.name: Proof of TP11.7
nodes.statement: Apply JL (Theorem~\ref{jl_transform}) to reduce dimension to $O_c(\log n)$; bound preprocessing/query running time of one two-level table; use Lemma~\ref{lower_coll_lemma} for success probability $Q$; build $1/Q$ independent copies; convert expected to worst-case query time via Markov; minimize over $\tau$ at $\tau=\sqrt{2}$ to obtain $\rho \le 7/(8c^2)+O(1/c^3)+o_c(1)$.

nodes.name: JL dimension reduction
nodes.statement: Apply Theorem~\ref{jl_transform} to reduce $\ell_2^d$ to $\ell_2^{O_c(\log n)}$ in time $O_c(nd\log n)$, increasing failure probability by an arbitrarily small constant.

nodes.name: Bound preprocessing and query time
nodes.statement: Preprocessing is $O_c(n^{1+o_{c,\tau}(1)})$ plus $O_c(n^2\log n)$ for the diameter-pruning lines 5--7 plus $O_c(n\log^{O(1)} n)$ for computing $u_i$ via~\cite{gls-gaco-88}. Query time is $O_c(n^{o_{c,\tau}(1)}+d\log n)$ in expectation by Lemma~\ref{upper_coll_lemma}.

nodes.name: Success probability and replication
nodes.statement: Lemma~\ref{lower_coll_lemma} gives $\Pr[\text{success}] \ge Q = n^{-(1-\frac{1}{2\tau^2}+\frac{1}{2\tau^4})/c^2+O_\tau(1/c^3)+o_{c,\tau}(1)}$. Build $1/Q$ independent copies to make success probability constant.

nodes.name: Worst-case query time via Markov
nodes.statement: Modify the algorithm to stop after $3/Q+1$ inspected non-near-neighbors. By Markov's inequality the algorithm fails to inspect a near neighbor with probability $\le 1/3$, and across $1/Q$ tables the joint failure probability is $\le (1-Q)^{1/Q} \le 1/e$, giving overall success probability $\ge 1-1/3-1/e$.

nodes.name: Optimize $\tau$
nodes.statement: Minimize $\rho(\tau) = (1-\frac{1}{2\tau^2}+\frac{1}{2\tau^4})/c^2+\ldots$ at $\tau = \sqrt{2}$, yielding $\rho \le 7/(8c^2)+O(1/c^3)+o_c(1)$.

nodes.name: Quasi-linear preprocessing variant
nodes.statement: If quasi-linear preprocessing time is desired, modify Algorithm~\ref{two_level_hashing_alg} by picking an arbitrary point $p \in B_i$ and removing all points further than $\tau c$ from $p$; this achieves $\rho \le 15/(16c^2)+O(1/c^3)+o_c(1)$ with preprocessing time $O_c(n^{1+\rho}+nd\log n)$.

nodes.name: $\ell_1$ / Hamming consequence
nodes.statement: By the classical $\ell_1$-to-$\ell_2^2$ reduction, the main theorem yields a data structure for the Hamming space and $\ell_1$ norm with $\rho \le 7/(8c)+O(1/c^{3/2})+o_c(1)$, the first improvement over Indyk-Motwani 1998.

nodes.name: Bypassing the OWZ LSH lower bound
nodes.statement: Standard LSH satisfies $\rho \ge 1/c - o_c(1)$ for $\ell_1$ (O'Donnell-Wu-Zhou 2011); the data-aware two-level scheme is not a single LSH family, so this lower bound does not apply, allowing the improvement.
